concepts.label: Respiring organisms take up oxygen; with the carbon dioxide absorbed, the gas around them shrinks by the oxygen used

objectives.statement: Measure the rate of oxygen uptake with a respirometer
Explain the controls and the result

title.default: Respirometer: oxygen uptake by germinating seeds

summary.default: Measure the oxygen taken up by germinating peas in a respirometer over soda lime, with boiled peas, a thermobarometer of glass beads, and peas without soda lime as controls.

briefing.default: Put 3 g of soda lime in each tube under a gauze and 5 g of peas on it (or glass beads, or nothing over the soda lime for the thermobarometer). Seal each tube with the capillary bung, stand them in the water bath at 25 °C with the screw clips open for 10 minutes to reach the temperature, close the clips, read the scale, and read it again 10 minutes later. Oxygen uptake = fall in gas volume ÷ time ÷ mass.

runs.default: =[['live','Germinating peas over soda lime','bio:germinating-peas',true,false,25],['dead','Boiled peas over soda lime','bio:boiled-peas',true,false,25],['beads','Glass beads over soda lime (thermobarometer)','',true,true,25],['no-lime','Germinating peas, no soda lime','bio:germinating-peas',false,false,25]]

compareObjective.default: Compare oxygen uptake by living and dead seeds, and with and without soda lime

default.prompt: Why does the drop hardly move when there is no soda lime?

options.label: The seeds give out about as much carbon dioxide as the oxygen they take up, so the volume of gas stays nearly the same
Without soda lime the seeds cannot respire

predicates.statement: Germinating peas take up oxygen; boiled peas and glass beads do not; without soda lime the volume hardly changes
predicates.check: first(recorded('uptake live')) > 0.002 && abs(first(recorded('uptake dead'))) < 0.0005 && abs(first(recorded('uptake beads'))) < 0.0005 && abs(first(recorded('uptake no-lime'))) < 0.2 * first(recorded('uptake live'))

predicates.statement: The control without soda lime is explained

expectedObservations.statement: Germinating peas take up about 0.006 mL of oxygen per gram a minute at 25 °C

variants.title: Respirometer: seeds and small animals
variants.summary: Compare the oxygen uptake per gram of germinating peas, woodlice and maggots in respirometers over soda lime, with a thermobarometer.
variants.briefing: As for germinating seeds, with 5 g of woodlice or maggots on the gauze instead (handle them gently; return them after the experiment). Express each rate per gram so the organisms can be compared.

values.compareObjective: Compare the rates of respiration of different organisms

question.prompt: Why do maggots take up oxygen faster per gram than woodlice?

options.label: They are growing fast and very active, so they need more ATP per gram
They react with the soda lime

predicates.statement: Maggots respire fastest per gram; the thermobarometer does not move
predicates.check: first(recorded('uptake maggots')) > first(recorded('uptake peas')) && first(recorded('uptake maggots')) > first(recorded('uptake woodlice')) && abs(first(recorded('uptake beads'))) < 0.0005

expectedObservations.statement: Woodlice take up about 0.005 mL per gram a minute

variants.title: Respirometer: the effect of temperature on respiration
variants.summary: Measure the oxygen uptake of germinating peas over soda lime at 25, 30, 35 and 40 °C and find the temperature coefficient Q10.
variants.briefing: As for germinating seeds, with each tube in a water bath at a different temperature. Q10 = rate at (T + 10) ÷ rate at T.

values.compareObjective: Relate the rate of respiration to temperature

question.prompt: Why does the rate about double for each 10 °C rise?

options.label: Respiration is catalysed by enzymes, whose reactions speed up as more molecules have enough energy to react

predicates.statement: The rate rises with temperature, with Q10 between 1.6 and 3 from 25 to 35 °C
predicates.check: first(recorded('uptake t25')) < first(recorded('uptake t30')) && first(recorded('uptake t30')) < first(recorded('uptake t35')) && first(recorded('uptake t35')) < first(recorded('uptake t40')) && first(recorded('uptake t35')) / first(recorded('uptake t25')) > 1.6 && first(recorded('uptake t35')) / first(recorded('uptake t25')) < 3

expectedObservations.statement: At 40 °C the peas take up about twice as much as at 30 °C
